what: Sizing the Windows decode pool to the performance-core count instead of the raw physical-core count on a hybrid Intel host. A/B of one binary with the policy default-on vs CAMELID_WIN_HYBRID_POLICY=off, plus a width sweep, a placement sweep, and a replication attempt under memory pressure.
lever: hybrid decode width (default-on, Intel + multi-EfficiencyClass only); kill switch CAMELID_WIN_HYBRID_POLICY=0|false|off|no
supersedes: p1-cpu-thread-sweep-llama3b-20260621T2150Z.json, whose host was an i7-11800H 8C/16T -- a non-hybrid part where physical-core count and performance-core count are the same number.
host: win i9-14900HX 8P+16E (24 physical / 32 logical), RTX 4060 Laptop present but CPU decode forced

method.sampling_unit: one server process (the decode pool is built once per process)
method.pairing: arms randomized within each rep, compared paired
method.env: CAMELID_CUDA_RESIDENT_DECODE=0 throughout (resident CUDA decode is on by default when a device is present and would decide the result instead of the thread policy)

results.note: Free memory 7.25-7.84 GB, server RSS 1.77 GB. Absolute values on this host move strongly with free memory; the paired randomized arms are what make the comparison survive that.

ttft_s.note: prefill is untouched and keeps its own wider pool

width_sweep.note: Answers 'why EfficiencyClass rather than any number below physical'. Baseline is the shipped default (24).

4.note: worse than shipping nothing -- under-selection is a NEGATIVE direction

placement_sweep.note: Why this lever ships NO pinning. Compared against the identically-sized pool left unpinned. CAMELID_WIN_PIN is left byte-identical to main.

parity.why: decode parallelises over independent output rows with serial per-row reductions, so pool width cannot change the arithmetic

gpu_host.note: With resident CUDA decode driving decode the pool width is irrelevant.

verdict: Ships default-on for GenuineIntel hosts reporting more than one EfficiencyClass: +16.7% decode, -55.3% CPU seconds, byte-identical output, TTFT unmoved. CAMELID_WIN_HYBRID_POLICY=off restores the previous width exactly.
open_questions: Whether the performance-core count is the right width on a differently shaped hybrid part (2P+8E, 4P+4E) is unmeasured; the policy would build a 2- or 4-wide pool there and the sweep measures 4 as negative.

AMD is gated out by a CPUID vendor check rather than measured: Zen 5c compact cores and multi-CCD desktop parts also report more than one EfficiencyClass without being a P/E split. The gate comes off when an AMD host is measured.
The per-host optimum stays deferred to GAIT; this receipt only replaces a default derived on a non-hybrid part with one derived on a hybrid part.
